LESSON: A dispatch naming four target classes can hide sub-classes with completely different acquisition postures -- 'utilityService' looked like one rail and turned out to be three separate sourcing decisions (water/sewer strong, electric weak, gas nonexistent). Worth decomposing a declared-ahead rail's real acquisition shape before carding it, not assuming uniformity from the rail name.

A fetcher returning 402/403/404/DNS-failure on a primary government source page is common for these portals (Cloudflare/bot protection) and is not evidence the underlying data doesn't exist -- always look for a downstream mirror (state agency cross-publication, county GIS re-hosting, ArcGIS Hub listing) before concluding a source is unreachable.

When multiple independent mirrors of the same underlying dataset are found (e.g. PUCT CCN via TWDB/Harris County/Esri Hub, or TEA/TLC school districts vs NCES EDGE), their near-matching feature counts are a genuinely useful corroboration signal, cheap to check via a returnCountOnly query, and worth doing even when not strictly required by the dispatch.
